question: What does the Catholic Church teach about abortion?
answer_md: The Church teaches that human life must be respected and protected absolutely from the moment of conception. From the first moment of his or her existence, a human being has the rights of a person, above all the right to life. Direct abortion, willed as an end or a means, is gravely contrary to the moral law. The Church also offers mercy, healing and forgiveness to all who regret an abortion, and support to mothers in difficulty.

question: What is Advent?
answer_md: Advent is the four-week season that begins the Church’s year. It prepares us for Christmas, when we remember Christ’s first coming at Bethlehem, and it turns our hearts to his second coming at the end of time. Its colour is violet, with rose on the third Sunday (Gaudete Sunday). It is a season of joyful, hopeful waiting, prayer and conversion.

question: Do angels really exist?
answer_md: Yes. The existence of angels, spiritual beings without bodies, is a truth of faith witnessed throughout Scripture and Tradition. They are personal and immortal creatures with intelligence and will, who glorify God and serve his plan of salvation. They are God’s messengers, as Gabriel was to Mary.

question: Does everyone have a guardian angel?
answer_md: The Church teaches that from infancy to death human life is surrounded by the watchful care and intercession of angels. Jesus said of little ones that “their angels in heaven always behold the face of my Father.” Catholics celebrate the Holy Guardian Angels on 2 October and often pray the “Angel of God” prayer.

question: What is an annulment?
answer_md: An annulment (a declaration of nullity) is not a Catholic divorce. It is a finding by a Church tribunal, after careful study, that a valid marriage never existed because something essential was missing on the wedding day, such as free consent. A valid sacramental marriage, once consummated, cannot be dissolved by any human power.
sources: CCC 1629, 1640; Mark 10:9; Code of Canon Law 1095–1103

question: What is the Anointing of the Sick?
answer_md: It is the sacrament by which the Church commends the seriously ill or elderly to the suffering and glorified Lord, that he may raise them up and save them. The priest anoints the forehead and hands with blessed oil. It gives strength, peace and courage, forgives sins if the person cannot confess, and sometimes restores bodily health. It is not only for the dying.

question: What is the Apostles’ Creed?
answer_md: The Apostles’ Creed is an ancient summary of the Christian faith, rightly considered a faithful summary of the apostles’ teaching. It is the baptismal creed of the Church of Rome and is prayed at the beginning of the Rosary. It professes faith in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, the Church, the forgiveness of sins and eternal life.

question: What is apostolic succession?
answer_md: The apostles chose men to succeed them, handing on their authority by the laying on of hands. Bishops are the successors of the apostles in an unbroken line. Through them the Church keeps the faith and the sacraments that Christ entrusted to the apostles.

question: Why do Catholics receive ashes on Ash Wednesday?
answer_md: Ashes are a biblical sign of repentance and of our mortality. On Ash Wednesday, the first day of Lent, the priest marks our foreheads with ashes, saying “Repent, and believe in the Gospel” or “Remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return.” It is a day of fasting and abstinence.

question: What is the Assumption of Mary?
answer_md: The Assumption is the truth that at the end of her earthly life the Virgin Mary was taken up body and soul into heavenly glory. Pope Pius XII defined it as dogma in 1950. Mary shares in a unique way in her Son’s Resurrection, and her Assumption anticipates the resurrection of all Christians. It is celebrated on 15 August.

question: What does Baptism do?
answer_md: Baptism is the first sacrament and the gateway to the others. It frees us from original sin and all personal sin, makes us children of God and members of Christ and his Church, and gives us a share in Christ’s priesthood. It leaves a permanent spiritual mark, so it can never be repeated.

question: Why do Catholics baptise babies?
answer_md: Children are born with a fallen human nature and need the new birth of Baptism. The Church baptises infants because grace is a free gift that does not depend on our merit, and parents would deny a child a priceless gift by delaying it. Infant Baptism is an immemorial practice; Scripture tells of whole households being baptised.

question: Can anyone baptise in an emergency?
answer_md: Yes. Normally a bishop, priest or deacon baptises. In case of necessity, anyone, even a non-baptised person, can baptise, provided they intend to do what the Church does and pour water on the person’s head while saying: “I baptise you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.”

question: What is Benediction?
answer_md: Benediction is a service of adoration in which the consecrated Host is placed in a monstrance on the altar. The faithful pray, sing hymns such as “O Salutaris” and “Tantum Ergo”, and the priest or deacon blesses the people with the Blessed Sacrament, making the sign of the cross.

question: Why does the Catholic Bible have more books?
answer_md: The Catholic Old Testament has 46 books, including Tobit, Judith, 1 and 2 Maccabees, Wisdom, Sirach and Baruch. These were part of the Greek Old Testament used by the early Church and were recognised by Church councils long before the Reformation. Some Protestant Bibles later removed them. The Catholic Bible has 73 books in all.

question: How should Catholics read the Bible?
answer_md: Catholics read Scripture as the Word of God written by human authors under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. We read it in the light of the whole Bible, the living Tradition of the Church and the harmony of the faith, paying attention to what the human authors intended. The Church urges all the faithful to read the Bible often.

question: What does a bishop do?
answer_md: Bishops are successors of the apostles. Each diocesan bishop teaches, sanctifies and governs the local Church entrusted to him, in communion with the Pope and the other bishops. Bishops receive the fullness of the sacrament of Holy Orders and can ordain priests and deacons.

question: Why is there a red lamp near the tabernacle?
answer_md: The sanctuary lamp burns near the tabernacle to show that Jesus is truly present in the Blessed Sacrament reserved there. That is why Catholics genuflect towards the tabernacle and keep a respectful silence in church.

question: What is the Catechism of the Catholic Church?
answer_md: The Catechism is an official, complete summary of Catholic teaching on faith and morals. Saint John Paul II published it in 1992. It has four parts: the Creed (what we believe), the Sacraments (how we celebrate), the Commandments (how we live) and Prayer (how we pray).

question: Why are Catholic priests celibate?
answer_md: In the Latin Church, priests are normally chosen from men who freely embrace celibacy “for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.” Celibacy is a sign of undivided devotion to Christ and to his people and points to the life of the world to come. It is a discipline, not a doctrine; Eastern Catholic Churches have married priests.

question: What are the Ten Commandments?
answer_md: 1. I am the Lord your God: you shall not have other gods. 2. You shall not take the name of the Lord in vain. 3. Keep holy the Lord’s Day. 4. Honour your father and mother. 5. You shall not kill. 6. You shall not commit adultery. 7. You shall not steal. 8. You shall not bear false witness. 9. You shall not covet your neighbour’s wife. 10. You shall not covet your neighbour’s goods.

question: What is the Communion of Saints?
answer_md: It is the union of all the faithful: those on earth, those being purified in purgatory and the saints in heaven. We are one family in Christ, so we can pray for one another, and the saints in heaven intercede for us.

question: Why do Catholics confess their sins to a priest?
answer_md: Jesus gave the apostles the power to forgive sins: “Whose sins you forgive are forgiven them.” The priest acts in the person of Christ. In Confession we hear with our own ears that we are forgiven, receive grace to grow, and are reconciled with God and the Church, since sin also wounds the Church.

question: Can a priest tell anyone what I said in Confession?
answer_md: Never. Every priest who hears confessions is bound under very severe penalties to keep absolute secrecy about the sins confessed. This is called the sacramental seal, and it admits no exceptions, even to save his own life.

question: How do I go to Confession?
answer_md: Examine your conscience first. Then, with the priest: make the sign of the cross; say how long it has been since your last confession; confess your sins honestly, mortal sins by kind and number; listen to the priest’s advice and penance; pray an act of contrition; receive absolution. Afterwards, do your penance.

question: What is Confirmation?
answer_md: Confirmation completes the grace of Baptism. The bishop (or a priest) anoints the forehead with chrism, saying “Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.” It roots us more deeply in God’s love, increases the gifts of the Holy Spirit and strengthens us to witness to Christ.

question: Must I always follow my conscience?
answer_md: A person must always obey the certain judgement of his conscience. But conscience must be formed, by God’s Word, prayer, the teaching of the Church and good advice, because it can be mistaken. We have a duty to form our conscience well.

question: Can a Catholic believe in evolution?
answer_md: The Church has no objection to scientific study of how life developed, provided we hold that God is Creator of all, that the human soul is created directly by God, and that human beings are not the product of chance. Faith and reason cannot truly contradict each other, since both come from God.

question: Why do Catholics make the sign of the cross?
answer_md: The sign of the cross is an ancient Christian prayer. By tracing the cross over ourselves “in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,” we profess the Trinity and the saving death of Jesus and ask for his protection. We begin and end prayers, and the day, with it.

question: Why do Catholic crosses show Jesus on them?
answer_md: A crucifix shows the body of Christ to remind us how much he loved us. Saint Paul said, “We preach Christ crucified.” Catholics also rejoice in the Resurrection; the crucifix keeps before our eyes the price of our salvation.

question: What is a deacon?
answer_md: Deacons receive the sacrament of Holy Orders “not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry.” They proclaim the Gospel, preach, baptise, witness marriages, conduct funerals and serve the poor. Some are preparing for the priesthood (transitional deacons); others, who may be married, remain deacons for life (permanent deacons).

question: What does the Church teach about the death penalty?
answer_md: In 2018 Pope Francis revised the Catechism to teach that the death penalty is inadmissible, because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The Church works for its abolition worldwide, while recognising the duty of the state to protect people by other effective means.

question: Does the devil exist?
answer_md: Yes. Satan is a fallen angel who freely and irrevocably rejected God. He tempts people, but his power is not infinite. He cannot prevent the building up of God’s Kingdom, and Christ has already conquered him by the Cross.

question: What is the Divine Mercy devotion?
answer_md: It comes from the revelations of Jesus to Saint Faustina Kowalska in Poland in the 1930s. It includes the image of Jesus with the words “Jesus, I trust in you,” the Chaplet of Divine Mercy, prayer at three o’clock, the hour of his death, and Divine Mercy Sunday, the Sunday after Easter, established by Saint John Paul II in 2000.

question: What is a Doctor of the Church?
answer_md: It is a title the Pope gives to saints whose teaching has greatly helped the whole Church, such as Augustine, Thomas Aquinas, Teresa of Avila and Thérèse of Lisieux. “Doctor” comes from the Latin for teacher.

question: Why is Easter the greatest Christian feast?
answer_md: Easter celebrates the Resurrection of Jesus, the crowning truth of our faith. By rising from the dead Christ conquered sin and death and opened eternal life to us. Every Sunday is a “little Easter”, and the Easter season lasts fifty days, until Pentecost.

question: What does the Church teach about other Christians?
answer_md: All who are baptised and believe in Christ are truly brothers and sisters in the Lord, though not in full communion with the Catholic Church. The Church prays and works for Christian unity, as Jesus prayed: “that they may all be one.”

question: Do Catholics really believe the Eucharist is Jesus?
answer_md: Yes. In the Eucharist the Body and Blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ are truly, really and substantially present. At the consecration the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ, though they still look and taste like bread and wine. Jesus said: “This is my body.”

question: How should I prepare to receive Holy Communion?
answer_md: A Catholic should be in a state of grace, without unconfessed mortal sin, and keep the Eucharistic fast of one hour from food and drink (water and medicine excepted). We approach with faith and reverence, answering “Amen” when the minister says “The Body of Christ.”
sources: CCC 1385–1388; 1 Corinthians 11:27–29; Code of Canon Law 919

question: What does the Church teach about euthanasia?
answer_md: Euthanasia, ending the life of sick, disabled or dying persons, is morally unacceptable. But it is not required to use extraordinary or burdensome treatments, and pain relief may be given even if it shortens life, as long as death is not intended. Palliative care is a special form of love.

question: What is an examination of conscience?
answer_md: It is a prayerful review of our thoughts, words and actions in the light of God’s Word, especially the Ten Commandments and the Beatitudes, to recognise our sins before Confession. Many Catholics also make a brief examination every night.

question: What is faith?
answer_md: Faith is both a gift of God and a free human act by which we believe God and everything he has revealed, because he is truth itself. It is a personal adherence to God and assent to what he reveals. Faith is necessary for salvation and must be lived out in love.

question: What are the Church’s rules on fasting and abstinence?
answer_md: Ash Wednesday and Good Friday are days of fasting and abstinence. Fasting (ages 18–59) means one full meal and two small meals that together do not make a full meal. Abstinence (age 14 and up) means no meat. Fridays are days of penance, with abstinence or another penance as the local bishops decide.

question: Why do Catholics call priests “Father”?
answer_md: Priests are spiritual fathers who bring people new life in Christ through the sacraments. Saint Paul wrote, “I became your father in Christ Jesus through the Gospel.” Jesus’ warning in Matthew 23:9 is against pride, not the word itself; Scripture often calls people “father”.

question: Did God give us free will?
answer_md: Yes. God created us free so that we could love him freely, since love cannot be forced. Freedom is the power to act or not to act, and to choose good. It reaches its perfection when directed to God; choosing evil is an abuse of freedom that leads to slavery to sin.

question: Why do Catholics genuflect?
answer_md: Bending the right knee to the floor is a sign of adoration before Jesus present in the Blessed Sacrament. “At the name of Jesus every knee should bend.”

question: Can we know God exists without the Bible?
answer_md: Yes. The Church teaches that God can be known with certainty from created things by the natural light of human reason. The order and beauty of the world and our longing for truth and goodness point to God. Revelation then tells us who God is and his plan of love.

question: Why is it called “Good” Friday?
answer_md: On Good Friday we remember the Passion and death of Jesus. It is “good” because by his death Christ saved us from sin and opened heaven. It is the only day of the year when Mass is not celebrated; instead there is the Celebration of the Lord’s Passion, with veneration of the cross.

question: What is grace?
answer_md: Grace is the free and undeserved help God gives us to respond to his call to become his children and share his divine life. Sanctifying grace is the gift of God’s life in the soul, received in Baptism. Actual graces are God’s help for particular moments.

question: What is heaven?
answer_md: Heaven is perfect life with the Most Holy Trinity, the Virgin Mary, the angels and all the saints. It is the fulfilment of our deepest longings, the state of supreme and lasting happiness. In heaven we will see God “face to face.”

question: Does the Church teach that hell exists?
answer_md: Yes. Hell is the state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God and the blessed. God predestines no one to hell; it is the result of freely choosing mortal sin and refusing God’s mercy until the end. The teaching is a call to responsibility and conversion.

question: What are holy days of obligation?
answer_md: Besides every Sunday, Catholics must attend Mass on certain great feasts. The universal list includes Christmas, Mary Mother of God, Epiphany, Ascension, Corpus Christi, the Assumption, All Saints, the Immaculate Conception, Saint Joseph and Saints Peter and Paul, but each bishops’ conference may move or reduce them. Check with your local diocese.

question: Who is the Holy Spirit?
answer_md: The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Holy Trinity, truly God, equal to the Father and the Son. He is the Lord and giver of life, who spoke through the prophets, came upon the apostles at Pentecost and lives in the Church and in every baptised person, making us holy.

question: What are the gifts of the Holy Spirit?
answer_md: The seven gifts are wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety and fear of the Lord. They are permanent dispositions that make us docile to the Holy Spirit. They are strengthened at Confirmation.

question: What are the fruits of the Holy Spirit?
answer_md: The Church lists twelve fruits: charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, generosity, gentleness, faithfulness, modesty, self-control and chastity. They are signs that the Holy Spirit is at work in a person’s life.

question: What is holy water for?
answer_md: Holy water is water blessed by a priest. It is a sacramental. Blessing ourselves with it at the church door reminds us of our Baptism, and it is used in blessings of people, homes and objects. It does not work like magic; it disposes us to receive grace.

question: Do Catholics worship statues?
answer_md: No. Catholics worship God alone. Statues, icons and images are like family photographs: they remind us of Jesus, Mary and the saints and lift our minds to them. The honour given to an image passes to the person it represents. God himself commanded images of cherubim for the Ark.

question: What is the Immaculate Conception?
answer_md: It is the truth that Mary, from the first moment of her conception, was preserved free from original sin by a singular grace of God, in view of the merits of Jesus Christ. It is not the conception of Jesus. Pope Pius IX defined it in 1854, and it is celebrated on 8 December.

question: What is the Incarnation?
answer_md: The Incarnation is the mystery that the eternal Son of God became man in the womb of the Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit. Jesus is one divine Person with two natures, truly God and truly man.

question: What is an indulgence?
answer_md: An indulgence is a remission before God of the temporal punishment due to sins already forgiven. The Church grants it through the merits of Christ and the saints, under conditions such as Confession, Holy Communion, prayer for the Pope’s intentions and a set prayer or good work. It can be gained for oneself or for the dead. Indulgences are never sold.

question: Does infallibility mean the Pope can never sin?
answer_md: No. The Pope is a sinner who goes to Confession like everyone. Infallibility means that when the Pope, as supreme teacher, solemnly defines a doctrine of faith or morals for the whole Church, the Holy Spirit protects him from error. This is used rarely.

question: Is Jesus God or man?
answer_md: Both. Jesus Christ is true God and true man, one divine Person with a divine nature and a human nature. He did not stop being God when he became man, and he truly lived, suffered, died and rose as one of us.

question: Why did Jesus have to die?
answer_md: Out of love, the Father sent his Son to reconcile us to himself. Jesus freely offered his life on the cross as a perfect sacrifice for the sins of the whole world, conquering sin and death and opening the way to eternal life.

question: Why is Saint Joseph so important?
answer_md: Joseph, the husband of Mary, was chosen by God to be the foster father of Jesus and guardian of the Holy Family. A just and faithful man, he obeyed God promptly. He is patron of the universal Church, of fathers, workers and a happy death. His feasts are 19 March and 1 May.

question: What happens when we die?
answer_md: At death the soul is separated from the body, and each person receives an immediate particular judgement: entrance into heaven, through purification (purgatory) if needed, or eternal separation from God (hell). At the end of time, at the Last Judgement, the dead will rise and Christ will come in glory.

question: What is the Kingdom of God?
answer_md: The Kingdom of God is God’s reign of love, justice and peace, which Jesus announced and made present by his words, miracles and above all his Death and Resurrection. The Church is its seed and beginning on earth; it will come in fullness at the end of time.

question: Why do Catholics kneel in church?
answer_md: Kneeling is a sign of humility, adoration and penitence before God. Catholics kneel during the Eucharistic Prayer, when the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ, and often after Holy Communion.

question: What is Lent?
answer_md: Lent is the forty days of preparation for Easter, from Ash Wednesday to the Mass of the Lord’s Supper on Holy Thursday. It recalls Jesus’ forty days in the desert. Through prayer, fasting and almsgiving we turn back to God and prepare to renew our baptismal promises at Easter.

question: Does the Church teach Limbo?
answer_md: Limbo was a theological opinion, never a defined doctrine. For children who die without Baptism, the Church entrusts them to the mercy of God, who desires all to be saved, and we may hope there is a way of salvation for them.

question: What do the colours of the priest’s vestments mean?
answer_md: Green is used in Ordinary Time (hope and growth); violet in Advent and Lent (preparation and penance); white or gold at Christmas, Easter and feasts of the Lord, Mary and non-martyr saints (joy and purity); red on Palm Sunday, Good Friday, Pentecost and feasts of martyrs and apostles (the Spirit and blood); rose on Gaudete and Laetare Sundays.
sources: General Instruction of the Roman Missal 346

question: What is the liturgy?
answer_md: The liturgy is the official public worship of the Church, above all the Mass and the sacraments, and also the Liturgy of the Hours. In it Christ continues the work of our redemption, and we join him in praising the Father.

question: Why is the Our Father so important?
answer_md: It is the prayer Jesus himself taught his disciples. Tertullian called it “the summary of the whole Gospel.” It has seven petitions: three for God’s glory and four for our needs. It is prayed at every Mass.

question: Why is marriage a sacrament?
answer_md: Christ raised marriage between a baptised man and woman to the dignity of a sacrament. Their covenant of lifelong, faithful and fruitful love becomes a sign of Christ’s love for his Church, and they receive grace to love each other and raise their children in faith.

question: Why do Catholics honour Mary?
answer_md: Mary is the Mother of Jesus, who is God, so she is the Mother of God. She is the first and most perfect disciple, full of grace. Catholics honour her as Scripture foretold: “all generations will call me blessed.” We do not worship her; we love her and ask her prayers, because she always leads us to her Son.

question: Why is Mary called the Mother of God?
answer_md: Because her Son, Jesus, is truly God. The Council of Ephesus in 431 confirmed this title (Theotokos, “God-bearer”). Elizabeth greeted her as “the mother of my Lord.” The title protects the truth that Jesus is one Person, God and man.

question: Did Mary have other children?
answer_md: The Church teaches that Mary remained a virgin all her life. The “brothers” of Jesus mentioned in the Gospels are close relatives; in Hebrew and Aramaic the same word was used for cousins and kin. James and Joses, called his brothers, were sons of another Mary.

question: What happens at Mass?
answer_md: The Mass makes present the one sacrifice of Christ on the cross and the meal of the Last Supper. It has two main parts: the Liturgy of the Word, where God speaks to us in Scripture, and the Liturgy of the Eucharist, where bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ and we receive him in Communion.

question: Why must Catholics go to Mass on Sunday?
answer_md: Sunday is the day of the Resurrection, the Lord’s Day. The third Commandment tells us to keep it holy, and from the beginning Christians gathered on the first day of the week for the Eucharist. Deliberately missing Sunday Mass without a serious reason, such as illness, is a grave sin.

question: Do miracles still happen?
answer_md: Yes. God can and does act beyond the ordinary course of nature, often in answer to prayer. The Church investigates claimed miracles very carefully, with doctors and scientists, for example before a saint is beatified or canonised.

question: What is a mortal sin?
answer_md: A mortal sin destroys charity in the heart. Three conditions must be met together: the matter is grave, the person knows it is seriously wrong, and the person freely chooses it. It must be confessed in the sacrament of Reconciliation.

question: What is the difference between mortal and venial sin?
answer_md: Venial sin is a less serious sin, or a serious matter without full knowledge or full consent. It weakens charity but does not break our friendship with God. Mortal sin breaks it. Venial sins are forgiven in many ways, including the Eucharist, but confessing them is strongly recommended.

question: What does the Church teach about family planning?
answer_md: Married couples may space births for serious reasons by using the natural rhythms of the woman’s fertility, which respects the meaning of married love. The Church teaches that contraception, which separates love from openness to life, is morally wrong.

question: What is the Nicene Creed?
answer_md: It is the profession of faith from the Councils of Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381), prayed at Sunday Mass. It states clearly that Jesus is “God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, consubstantial with the Father,” and that the Holy Spirit is “the Lord, the giver of life.”

question: What is a novena?
answer_md: A novena is nine days of prayer for a special intention or in preparation for a feast. It comes from the nine days the apostles prayed with Mary between the Ascension and Pentecost.

question: What is original sin?
answer_md: Original sin is the state of deprivation of original holiness and justice that all humanity inherits from the sin of our first parents. It is not a personal fault, but it leaves human nature wounded and inclined to sin. Baptism takes it away and gives us God’s life.

question: Why can only men be ordained priests?
answer_md: Jesus chose only men as his twelve apostles, and the apostles did the same when choosing their successors. The Church considers herself bound by this choice of the Lord. This is not about worth: men and women are equal in dignity, and women have always had indispensable roles in the Church.

question: What happened at Pentecost?
answer_md: Fifty days after Easter, the Holy Spirit came down on the apostles and Mary in the form of tongues of fire. The apostles began to proclaim Jesus boldly, and about three thousand people were baptised. Pentecost is often called the birthday of the Church.

question: Why do Catholics have a Pope?
answer_md: Jesus made Peter the rock of his Church and gave him the keys of the kingdom. The Pope, as Bishop of Rome, is Peter’s successor and the visible source and foundation of unity for the bishops and the whole Church.

question: How should I pray?
answer_md: Prayer is raising our mind and heart to God. Speak to him simply and honestly, listen in silence, read the Scriptures, and use the Church’s prayers. Prayer includes adoration, thanksgiving, sorrow for sin and asking for our needs and others’. Set a regular time each day.

question: What is the role of a priest?
answer_md: A priest receives the sacrament of Holy Orders to serve God’s people as a co-worker of the bishop. He celebrates Mass, forgives sins in Confession, anoints the sick, preaches the Word and cares for his people as a shepherd, acting in the person of Christ.

question: What is purgatory?
answer_md: Purgatory is a final purification for those who die in God’s grace and friendship but are still imperfectly purified. They are assured of eternal salvation, but need purification to enter the joy of heaven. We help them by prayer, especially the Mass.

question: Why do Catholics pray for the dead?
answer_md: Because love does not end at death, and those being purified can be helped by our prayers, almsgiving and above all the Mass. Scripture praises Judas Maccabeus for offering a sacrifice for the dead. November is especially dedicated to praying for the faithful departed.

question: Why is Mary called Queen of Heaven?
answer_md: Because she is the Mother of Christ the King and was taken up body and soul into heaven. In the kingdoms of Israel the mother of the king was queen. Her queenship is one of service and intercession, sharing in her Son’s reign. The feast of the Queenship of Mary is 22 August.

question: Why do Catholics adore the Eucharist outside Mass?
answer_md: Because Jesus remains truly present in the consecrated Host, reserved in the tabernacle. Eucharistic adoration is a way to spend time with him, thank him and pray. Jesus asked his friends, “Could you not watch with me one hour?”

question: What are relics?
answer_md: Relics are the bodies or parts of the bodies of saints, or objects they used. Catholics honour (never worship) relics because the saints’ bodies were temples of the Holy Spirit and will rise in glory. Scripture tells of healings through Elisha’s bones and cloths touched by Saint Paul.

question: Will our bodies rise again?
answer_md: Yes. We believe in the resurrection of the body. At the end of time, God will raise our bodies and reunite them with our souls, as Christ rose from the dead. The bodies of the just will be glorified.

question: What is the Rosary?
answer_md: The Rosary is a prayer in which we meditate on the life of Jesus with Mary, praying the Our Father, ten Hail Marys and the Glory Be for each mystery. There are four sets of mysteries: Joyful, Sorrowful, Glorious and Luminous. Popes have called it a summary of the whole Gospel.

question: Which Rosary mysteries are prayed on each day?
answer_md: Joyful mysteries on Monday and Saturday; Sorrowful on Tuesday and Friday; Glorious on Wednesday and Sunday; Luminous on Thursday.

question: What are sacramentals?
answer_md: Sacramentals are sacred signs instituted by the Church, such as blessings, holy water, rosaries, medals, scapulars and blessed candles. They do not give grace as the sacraments do, but they prepare us to receive grace and help us sanctify everyday life.

question: What are the seven sacraments?
answer_md: Baptism, Confirmation and the Eucharist (sacraments of initiation); Penance and the Anointing of the Sick (sacraments of healing); Holy Orders and Matrimony (sacraments at the service of communion). They are effective signs of grace, instituted by Christ, by which divine life is given to us.

question: Why do Catholics pray to saints?
answer_md: We do not pray to saints in place of God. We ask them to pray for us, as we ask friends on earth to pray for us. The saints are alive in Christ and close to God, and “the prayer of a righteous man has great power.”

question: How does someone become a saint?
answer_md: After a person’s death, the Church may study their life. If they lived heroic virtue, they are declared Venerable. With a verified miracle through their intercession they are beatified (Blessed); with a second miracle, canonised (Saint). Martyrs can be beatified without a miracle. The Church does not make saints; it recognises them.

question: What is the brown scapular?
answer_md: The brown scapular is a sacramental of the Carmelite family: two small pieces of cloth worn over the shoulders, a sign of consecration to Mary and of trust in her protection. Tradition links it with Saint Simon Stock (1251). It is not a charm; it is a commitment to live as a Christian.

question: Why do Catholics rely on Tradition, not only the Bible?
answer_md: Before the New Testament was written, the apostles handed on the faith by preaching. The Word of God comes to us through Sacred Scripture and Sacred Tradition, both from the same divine source. Saint Paul told Christians to hold fast to traditions taught “by word of mouth or by letter.”

question: Do Catholics believe Jesus will come again?
answer_md: Yes. Christ will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead, and his Kingdom will have no end. No one knows the day or the hour, so we live ready, watching and praying.

question: What is sin?
answer_md: Sin is an offence against God, a failure in genuine love for God and neighbour caused by a perverse attachment to certain goods. It wounds human nature and solidarity. God’s mercy is greater than any sin for those who repent.

question: Why do Christians worship on Sunday, not Saturday?
answer_md: Jesus rose from the dead on the first day of the week, Sunday. The first Christians gathered to break bread on that day, the “Lord’s Day,” which fulfils the meaning of the Jewish Sabbath.

question: What are faith, hope and charity?
answer_md: They are the three theological virtues, given by God and directed to God. Faith believes God and what he has revealed; hope desires heaven and trusts in God’s help; charity loves God above all things and our neighbour as ourselves. “The greatest of these is love.”

question: Must Catholics give money to the Church?
answer_md: Yes. One of the precepts of the Church is to help provide for the needs of the Church according to one’s ability. There is no fixed percentage for all; giving generously of our time, talents and money is a sign of gratitude to God.

question: What does transubstantiation mean?
answer_md: It is the word the Church uses for the change that takes place at the consecration of the Mass: the whole substance of the bread becomes the Body of Christ, and the whole substance of the wine becomes his Blood, while their appearances remain.

question: What is the Holy Trinity?
answer_md: The Trinity is the central mystery of Christian faith: one God in three divine Persons, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. They are not three gods but one, each fully God, distinct in their relations. We know this only because God revealed it.

question: Why is the Church called One, Holy, Catholic and Apostolic?
answer_md: These are the four marks of the Church. She is one, united in faith, sacraments and leadership; holy, because Christ makes her holy; catholic, meaning universal, sent to all peoples; and apostolic, built on the apostles and their successors.

question: Do I need to confess venial sins?
answer_md: It is not strictly necessary, but the Church strongly recommends it. Regular confession of everyday faults helps us form our conscience, fight bad tendencies, let ourselves be healed by Christ and grow in the life of the Spirit.

question: What are the cardinal virtues?
answer_md: Prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance. They are called “cardinal” (from the Latin for hinge) because all other moral virtues hinge on them. They help us live good lives with ease and joy.

question: What is a vocation?
answer_md: A vocation is God’s call. Every Christian is called to holiness. Within this, God calls each person to a particular way of life: marriage, the priesthood, religious life or consecrated single life. We discover it through prayer, the sacraments and good guidance.

question: What are the works of mercy?
answer_md: The corporal works: feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, clothe the naked, shelter the homeless, visit the sick, visit the imprisoned and bury the dead. The spiritual works: counsel the doubtful, instruct the ignorant, admonish sinners, comfort the afflicted, forgive offences, bear wrongs patiently and pray for the living and the dead.

question: What is the difference between worship and honour?
answer_md: Worship (adoration, in Latin latria) is given to God alone. The honour given to the saints is called veneration (dulia), and the special honour given to Mary is called hyperdulia. Honouring God’s friends glorifies God, who made them holy.

question: Is it wrong to write “Xmas”?
answer_md: Not in itself. X is the Greek letter chi, the first letter of Christos, Christ, and Christians have used it as a symbol of Christ for centuries, as in the Chi-Rho (XP). Still, writing “Christmas” in full keeps Christ clearly at the centre.

question: Why don’t Catholics say “Yahweh” in the liturgy?
answer_md: Out of reverence. Following ancient Jewish practice, the Church does not pronounce the sacred four-letter name of God (YHWH) in the liturgy, but says “the Lord” instead. In 2008 the Holy See asked that this be observed in prayers and songs at Mass.
sources: Congregation for Divine Worship, letter of 29 June 2008; CCC 209

question: What does it mean to have zeal for God?
answer_md: Zeal is burning love for God and his glory that moves us to serve him and bring others to him. Jesus showed it when he cleansed the Temple: “Zeal for your house will consume me.” Christian zeal is always joined to charity and humility.

question: What does the Advent wreath mean?
answer_md: The evergreen circle stands for God’s everlasting love. Its four candles, three violet and one rose, are lit one by one on the Sundays of Advent, as the light grows brighter while we wait for Christ, the Light of the world. The rose candle is lit on Gaudete Sunday.

question: What is almsgiving?
answer_md: Almsgiving is giving to the poor out of love for God and neighbour. With prayer and fasting, it is one of the three traditional practices of penance, especially in Lent. Jesus taught us to give quietly, without seeking praise.

question: Why is the altar so important in a Catholic church?
answer_md: The altar is the place where the sacrifice of the cross is made present in the Mass, and the table of the Lord to which the people are invited. It is a symbol of Christ himself, so the priest kisses it at the start and end of Mass.

question: What are the Beatitudes?
answer_md: They are the eight blessings Jesus taught at the start of the Sermon on the Mount, beginning “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” They describe the heart of a disciple and the happiness God promises.

question: Is the Bible without error?
answer_md: The Church teaches that, since God is the author of Scripture through inspired human writers, the books of the Bible teach firmly, faithfully and without error the truth God wanted put into writing for the sake of our salvation.

question: Why do Catholics light candles in church?
answer_md: A candle is a sign of prayer rising to God and of Christ, the Light of the world. Lighting a votive candle before a statue or icon is a way of continuing our prayer after we leave. Candles are also used at Mass, Baptism and funerals.

question: What is charity?
answer_md: Charity is the theological virtue by which we love God above all things for his own sake, and our neighbour as ourselves for the love of God. It is the greatest of the virtues and the soul of every other.

question: What does the Church teach about chastity?
answer_md: Chastity is the virtue that integrates our sexuality within the whole person, so that we can love truly. Everyone is called to chastity according to their state of life: married couples by faithfulness, single people by continence. It is a source of freedom and joy.

question: Can someone be saved outside the Catholic Church?
answer_md: The Church teaches that all salvation comes from Christ through his Church. Those who, through no fault of their own, do not know Christ or his Church, but seek God sincerely and try to do his will as their conscience tells them, may also attain eternal salvation.

question: Can non-Catholics receive Holy Communion?
answer_md: Receiving Communion is a sign of full unity in faith with the Catholic Church, so normally only Catholics in a state of grace receive. Other Christians are warmly welcome at Mass and may come forward for a blessing. There are rare exceptions set by Church law.

question: What is Corpus Christi?
answer_md: Corpus Christi, the Solemnity of the Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ, honours Jesus’ presence in the Eucharist. Many parishes hold a Eucharistic procession through the streets on this day.

question: Why did God create the world?
answer_md: God created the world out of love, not out of need, to show forth and share his glory, goodness and happiness. Everything he made is good, and he created human beings in his image, to know and love him.

question: Why do Catholics hold a funeral Mass?
answer_md: At a funeral Mass the Church commends the dead person to God’s mercy, prays for their purification, and comforts the family with the hope of the resurrection. Christ’s victory over death gives Christian death a positive meaning.

question: Is there any sin God cannot forgive?
answer_md: There is no sin, however serious, that God will not forgive to anyone who truly repents. The “sin against the Holy Spirit” is a deliberate refusal to accept his mercy; it is unforgivable only because the person rejects forgiveness.

question: Is gossip a sin?
answer_md: Yes. Detraction (revealing someone’s faults without a valid reason) and calumny (spreading lies about them) harm a person’s reputation, which everyone has a right to. They offend against the eighth commandment, and harm done should be repaired.

question: Who is the Holy Family?
answer_md: Jesus, Mary and Joseph. Their home in Nazareth is the model for every Christian family, a “domestic church” of prayer, work and love. The Feast of the Holy Family is celebrated in the Christmas season.

question: What is Christian hope?
answer_md: Hope is the theological virtue by which we desire heaven and eternal life as our happiness, trusting in Christ’s promises and relying on the help of the Holy Spirit, not on our own strength.

question: What is Lectio Divina?
answer_md: Lectio Divina (“divine reading”) is a slow, prayerful reading of Scripture in four steps: read a passage, meditate on it, respond in prayer, and rest in God in contemplation. It is an ancient way to let God speak to us through his Word.

question: Why do Catholics give something up for Lent?
answer_md: Giving up something we enjoy is a small act of penance that unites us with Christ’s forty days of fasting, trains us in self-control and makes room for God and for the poor. It is best joined to more prayer and generosity.

question: What does it mean to consecrate oneself to Jesus through Mary?
answer_md: It means entrusting oneself completely to Jesus through Mary, the surest way to him, as taught by Saint Louis de Montfort. Saint John Paul II took the motto “Totus Tuus” (“Totally yours”) from this devotion.

question: What should I wear to Mass?
answer_md: There is no uniform, but our clothing should show respect for the Lord we meet. Modest, tidy clothes, according to local custom, help us and others to pray. What matters most is a heart prepared to worship.

question: What is the Year of Mercy or a Jubilee?
answer_md: A Jubilee or Holy Year is a special year of grace proclaimed by the Pope, usually every 25 years, with pilgrimages, the opening of Holy Doors and opportunities for forgiveness and renewal. Pope Francis proclaimed an extraordinary Jubilee of Mercy in 2015–2016, and an ordinary Jubilee of Hope in 2025.

question: Why do Catholics go on pilgrimage?
answer_md: A pilgrimage is a prayerful journey to a holy place, such as Jerusalem, Rome, Lourdes or a local shrine. It expresses our life as a journey to God, and is a time for prayer, penance and conversion.

question: What are the precepts of the Church?
answer_md: They are minimum duties for Catholics: attend Mass on Sundays and holy days; confess serious sins at least once a year; receive Communion at least during the Easter season; observe the days of fasting and abstinence; and help provide for the needs of the Church.

question: Do Catholics believe in the “rapture”?
answer_md: The Church does not teach a secret rapture before the end. Catholics believe that Christ will come again visibly in glory to judge the living and the dead, and that the faithful will be caught up to meet him at that one Second Coming.

question: What are religious brothers and sisters?
answer_md: They are men and women who consecrate their lives to God by the vows of poverty, chastity and obedience, usually living in community under a rule, such as Benedictines, Franciscans or Carmelites. They serve through prayer, teaching, nursing, mission and more.

question: How should Catholics keep Sunday holy?
answer_md: By attending Mass, and by resting from unnecessary work and business, making time for God, family, rest, works of mercy and the care of the sick and elderly.

question: What is devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus?
answer_md: It honours the heart of Jesus as the symbol of his boundless love for us. Jesus revealed his Heart to Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque in the 1670s and asked for acts of reparation, such as Holy Communion on the first Friday of each month.

question: Why does God allow suffering?
answer_md: This is a mystery, and no quick answer is enough. God does not cause evil, but permits it and can draw good from it. Jesus took suffering on himself on the cross and gives it meaning. We can unite our sufferings to his, and he promises to wipe away every tear.

question: What is the difference between Tradition and traditions?
answer_md: Sacred Tradition (capital T) is the living transmission of the faith from the apostles, which cannot change. Small-t traditions are customs and practices, such as particular devotions or disciplines, which the Church can adapt over time.

question: What is the Vatican?
answer_md: Vatican City is the smallest independent state in the world, inside Rome. It is the home of the Pope and the centre of the Church’s government, the Holy See. Saint Peter’s Basilica is built over the tomb of the apostle Peter.

question: What is the place of women in the Church?
answer_md: Women and men are equal in dignity, both made in God’s image. Women have always had indispensable roles: Mary, the Mother of God; the women who first witnessed the Resurrection; foundresses, martyrs, mothers, teachers and four women Doctors of the Church.

question: What is the Angelus?
answer_md: The Angelus is a short prayer recalling the Incarnation, traditionally prayed at 6am, noon and 6pm when church bells ring. It has three verses about the Annunciation, each followed by a Hail Mary, and a closing prayer. In the Easter season it is replaced by the Regina Caeli.

question: What is an Act of Contrition?
answer_md: An Act of Contrition is a prayer telling God we are sorry for our sins, firmly intending not to sin again, and trusting in his mercy. It is said in Confession and can be prayed at any time, especially at night. A common form begins: “O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended thee…”

question: Must Catholics believe in apparitions such as Lourdes or Fatima?
answer_md: No. Approved apparitions are “private revelations”. The Church may judge them worthy of belief and helpful for faith, but they add nothing to the Revelation completed in Christ, and Catholics are not obliged to believe them. Their purpose is to help us live the Gospel more fully.

question: Which Bible translation should Catholics use?
answer_md: Catholics should use a translation with the full 73 books, approved by the Church (it usually carries an imprimatur). Well-known Catholic translations include the Douay-Rheims, the Revised Standard Version Catholic Edition, the New American Bible and the Jerusalem Bible. Your bishops’ conference approves the version used at Mass.

question: Where should I start reading the Bible?
answer_md: A good place to begin is one of the Gospels, such as Mark or Luke, which tell the life of Jesus. Then read the Acts of the Apostles, a few Psalms, and Genesis. Read slowly and prayerfully, asking the Holy Spirit to help you, and follow the daily Mass readings to read with the whole Church.

question: Does the Church allow cremation?
answer_md: Yes. The Church prefers burial, following the example of Christ, but allows cremation as long as it is not chosen for reasons against Christian faith. The ashes should be kept in a sacred place, such as a cemetery or church columbarium, not scattered, divided or kept at home.

question: Can a divorced Catholic receive Holy Communion?
answer_md: Divorce itself does not stop a Catholic from receiving Communion. A divorced person who has not entered a new union can receive the sacraments. Those who have remarried without an annulment should speak with their priest, who can help them understand their situation and the path of accompaniment the Church offers.

question: Who can be a godparent?
answer_md: A godparent should be a practising Catholic, at least sixteen, confirmed, who has received First Communion, and lives a life of faith. A baptised non-Catholic Christian may act as a Christian witness together with a Catholic godparent. Parents cannot be godparents for their own child.

question: Can a Catholic marry someone who is not Catholic?
answer_md: Yes, with permission from the bishop, usually arranged through the parish. Marriage to a baptised Christian of another denomination is called a mixed marriage; marriage to a non-baptised person needs a dispensation. The Catholic promises to keep the faith and do all they can to raise the children Catholic.

question: How do Catholics prepare for marriage?
answer_md: Couples should contact their parish several months before the wedding (often six to twelve). Preparation usually includes meetings with the priest, a marriage preparation course, paperwork such as baptism certificates, and time to pray together. It is a chance to build the marriage on Christ, not only to plan the wedding day.

question: At what age do Catholics receive First Holy Communion?
answer_md: In the Latin Church, children usually receive First Communion around the age of reason, about seven, after preparation and their first Confession. In Eastern Catholic Churches, infants receive Communion together with Baptism and Confirmation.

question: At what age are Catholics confirmed?
answer_md: In the Latin Church, Confirmation is usually given around the age of reason or later, according to the norms of each bishops’ conference, often between seven and sixteen. Adults who were never confirmed can be confirmed after preparation. Eastern Catholics are confirmed (chrismated) at Baptism.

question: Can I receive Communion on the tongue or in the hand?
answer_md: Both are permitted in many countries, according to the norms of the bishops’ conference. Whichever way you receive, do so with reverence: bow before receiving, answer “Amen”, and consume the Host immediately in front of the minister.

question: Can I receive Holy Communion more than once a day?
answer_md: A Catholic may receive Communion a second time on the same day, but only within a Mass in which they take part. A person in danger of death may also receive Viaticum.

question: Is it a sin to miss Sunday Mass if I am sick?
answer_md: No. The Sunday obligation does not bind those excused for a serious reason, such as illness, caring for a sick person or young baby, or being unable to travel. It is good to pray at home, read the readings or follow a Mass broadcast, and make a spiritual communion.

question: What is a Mass intention?
answer_md: A Mass intention is a person or need for whom a Mass is offered, for example for someone who has died, a sick relative or a thanksgiving. People often give an offering (a stipend) when requesting it, which supports the priest; it is not a payment for grace.

question: Why are there three years of Sunday readings (Year A, B and C)?
answer_md: The Lectionary spreads the Bible over three years so that Catholics hear more of Scripture. Year A mainly uses Matthew’s Gospel, Year B Mark (with John), and Year C Luke. Weekdays follow a two-year cycle (Year I and II).
sources: Introduction to the Lectionary for Mass

question: Why does the Church still use Latin?
answer_md: Latin is the traditional language of the Latin Church and a sign of its unity across nations and centuries. Since Vatican II, Mass is usually celebrated in the language of the people, but Latin remains the official language of the liturgy and some Latin chants and prayers are encouraged.

question: What is the Liturgy of the Hours?
answer_md: The Liturgy of the Hours, or Divine Office, is the Church’s official daily prayer, made up of psalms, Scripture and prayers at different times of day, especially Morning Prayer and Evening Prayer. Priests and religious pray it daily, and lay people are warmly invited to join.

question: What is Ordinary Time?
answer_md: Ordinary Time is the part of the Church year outside the great seasons of Advent, Christmas, Lent and Easter. “Ordinary” comes from “ordinal”, meaning counted weeks. Its colour is green, a sign of hope and growth as we follow Jesus’ public life.
sources: General Norms for the Liturgical Year 43–44

question: What is the Easter Triduum?
answer_md: The Easter Triduum is the three holiest days of the year: from the Mass of the Lord’s Supper on Holy Thursday evening, through Good Friday and Holy Saturday, to Evening Prayer on Easter Sunday. It celebrates the Passion, death and Resurrection of Jesus as one great feast.
sources: General Norms for the Liturgical Year 18–21

question: What is the Easter Vigil?
answer_md: The Easter Vigil, on the night of Holy Saturday, is the greatest celebration of the year. It begins in darkness with the new fire and the Easter candle, continues with many Scripture readings, and celebrates Baptism and Confirmation of new Catholics before the Easter Eucharist.

question: Why is Christmas celebrated on 25 December?
answer_md: The Bible does not give the date of Jesus’ birth. Since at least the 4th century, the Church in Rome has celebrated it on 25 December, around the time of the winter solstice, when the days begin to grow longer: a fitting sign of Christ, the Light of the world.

question: How long is the Christmas season?
answer_md: The Christmas season begins on the evening of 24 December and continues until the feast of the Baptism of the Lord, in early or mid January. Catholics celebrate Christmas for the whole season, not just one day.
sources: General Norms for the Liturgical Year 32–38

question: What is the Epiphany?
answer_md: The Epiphany celebrates the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus, showing that he is the Saviour of all nations. It is celebrated on 6 January or, in many countries, on the Sunday between 2 and 8 January.

question: What is the Ascension?
answer_md: Forty days after his Resurrection, Jesus ascended into heaven in his risen body. He did not leave us alone: he sits at the right hand of the Father, intercedes for us, and sends the Holy Spirit. Many countries celebrate it on the following Sunday.

question: What are the “last rites”?
answer_md: The “last rites” usually means the sacraments for a dying person: Confession, the Anointing of the Sick and Holy Communion as Viaticum (“food for the journey”). If someone is seriously ill or dying, call a priest as soon as possible rather than waiting until the last moment.

question: What happens at the particular judgement?
answer_md: Immediately after death, each person is judged by Christ according to their faith and works. The soul then enters heaven (directly or after purification in purgatory) or chooses eternal separation from God. The Last Judgement at the end of time will reveal all things publicly.

question: What is an exorcism?
answer_md: An exorcism is a prayer in which the Church asks, in the name of Jesus, that a person or object be protected from the power of the evil one. A simple exorcism is part of Baptism. A major exorcism may be performed only by a priest with the bishop’s permission, after careful medical and spiritual discernment.

question: Can Catholics read horoscopes or consult fortune tellers?
answer_md: No. Horoscopes, astrology, fortune-telling and consulting mediums try to unveil the future or gain power apart from God. They contradict the trust and honour we owe to God alone. Catholics are invited to place their future in God’s providence.

question: What does the Church teach about charms and witchcraft?
answer_md: Magic, charms and sorcery, even when used to heal or protect, try to tame occult powers and are gravely contrary to the virtue of religion. Protection comes from God, through prayer, the sacraments and sacramentals, not from objects believed to work by themselves.

question: Is gambling a sin for Catholics?
answer_md: Games of chance and wagers are not in themselves wrong. They become wrong when they take money needed for one’s own or one’s family’s needs, or when they become an addiction. Moderation and responsibility are essential.

question: What does the Church teach about alcohol and drugs?
answer_md: Drinking alcohol in moderation is not wrong, but drunkenness is a sin against temperance and endangers oneself and others. Using drugs, except for medical reasons, gravely harms health and life. People struggling with addiction deserve compassion and help.

question: Can Catholics donate their organs?
answer_md: Yes. Organ donation after death is a noble act of generous love, encouraged by the Church, as long as free consent has been given. A donor must never be killed or have death hastened to obtain organs.

question: What does the Church teach about IVF?
answer_md: The Church understands the deep longing of couples for a child and supports research and treatments that help nature. It teaches that a child is a gift that should be conceived in the marital act itself, and so does not accept IVF, which separates conception from that act and often involves the loss of embryos.

question: What does the Church teach about those who die by suicide?
answer_md: Suicide is gravely contrary to the love of self, neighbour and God. But serious psychological disturbance, anguish or fear can greatly reduce responsibility. The Church does not despair of the salvation of those who have taken their own lives: God can provide a path to repentance, and we pray for them. If you are struggling, please speak to someone you trust or a local helpline today.

question: What does the Church teach about Judaism?
answer_md: The Jewish people were the first to hear the Word of God, and the Church has a unique bond with them. God’s gifts and call are irrevocable. Vatican II rejected every form of antisemitism and encouraged mutual respect and dialogue.

question: What does the Church teach about Muslims?
answer_md: The Church teaches that Muslims profess to hold the faith of Abraham and, together with Christians, adore the one, merciful God. Vatican II urged Christians and Muslims to forget past quarrels and to work together for justice, peace and freedom.

question: What is the difference between Catholics and the Orthodox?
answer_md: The Orthodox Churches share with Catholics the apostolic succession, the sacraments, and devotion to Mary. The main difference is that they are not in full communion with the Pope. The Catholic Church sees them as sister Churches and prays and works for full unity.

question: What are the Eastern Catholic Churches?
answer_md: The Eastern Catholic Churches, such as the Maronite, Ukrainian Greek Catholic, Syro-Malabar and Coptic Catholic Churches, are fully Catholic and in communion with the Pope, but celebrate their own ancient liturgies and traditions. Catholics may attend and receive the sacraments in any Catholic rite.

question: What is a patron saint?
answer_md: A patron saint is a saint chosen as a special intercessor and protector of a person, place, profession or cause, for example Saint Joseph for workers or Saint Cecilia for musicians. Catholics often take a patron saint’s name at Baptism or Confirmation.

question: What is a name day?
answer_md: A name day is the feast of the saint whose name a person bears. In many Catholic cultures it is celebrated like a birthday, as a reminder of the saint’s example and prayers.

question: Must a baby be given a saint’s name at Baptism?
answer_md: The Church asks that parents and godparents avoid names foreign to Christian sentiment. A saint’s name is a beautiful choice, giving the child a heavenly patron, but other good names may be given.

question: Who can be a Confirmation sponsor?
answer_md: A Confirmation sponsor must meet the same requirements as a godparent: a practising, confirmed Catholic, at least sixteen, who is not the candidate’s parent. It is fitting to choose one’s baptismal godparent.

question: What is a cardinal?
answer_md: A cardinal is a bishop (or priest) chosen by the Pope as a close adviser. Cardinals under eighty elect a new Pope in a conclave. They wear red as a sign of readiness to shed their blood for the faith.

question: What is a monsignor?
answer_md: Monsignor is an honorary title given by the Pope to some priests in recognition of their service. It does not add any sacramental power: a monsignor is a priest.

question: What is the difference between a nun and a sister?
answer_md: Strictly, a nun lives an enclosed, contemplative life in a monastery, devoted to prayer, while a religious sister lives an active life of service, such as teaching, nursing or caring for the poor. In everyday speech both words are often used for any woman religious.
sources: Code of Canon Law 667; Church practice

question: How is a new Pope elected?
answer_md: When the papacy is vacant, cardinals under eighty gather in the Sistine Chapel in a conclave. They pray and vote in secret until one candidate receives two-thirds of the votes. White smoke announces the election, and the new Pope is presented with the words “Habemus Papam”.

question: What is an encyclical?
answer_md: An encyclical is a letter from the Pope to the whole Church, and often to all people of good will, teaching on an important subject. Examples include Rerum Novarum (1891) on workers, Laudato Si’ (2015) on care for creation, and Deus Caritas Est (2005) on love.

question: What is Catholic social teaching?
answer_md: Catholic social teaching applies the Gospel to life in society. Its key principles include the dignity of every human person, the common good, solidarity, subsidiarity, the preferential option for the poor, the rights of workers, and care for creation.
sources: CCC 2419–2449; Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church

question: What does the Church teach about work and fair wages?
answer_md: Work is a way of sharing in God’s creation and serving others. Workers have a right to a just wage that allows them and their families to live a dignified life, to safe conditions, to rest, and to form associations. Refusing a just wage can be a grave injustice.

question: Why should Catholics care for the environment?
answer_md: Creation is God’s gift entrusted to our care, not ours to exploit. Caring for our “common home” is part of loving God and neighbour, especially the poor, who suffer most from environmental harm. Pope Francis wrote about this in Laudato Si’.

question: What does the Church teach about racism?
answer_md: Every human being is created in God’s image and has equal dignity. Every form of discrimination based on race, colour, sex, social condition, language or religion is incompatible with God’s plan and must be overcome.

question: Is it wrong to tell a “small” lie?
answer_md: Every lie, even a small one, offends against truth and charity, though not every lie is equally serious. We should speak the truth with kindness. Charity sometimes means keeping silent or keeping a secret, which is different from lying.

question: Is swearing or using God’s name carelessly a sin?
answer_md: The second commandment asks us to honour God’s name. Using it carelessly or in anger is wrong; blasphemy, speaking against God, the Church or the saints with hatred or contempt, is a grave sin. Rude words are also against charity and should be avoided.

question: What do adult children owe their parents?
answer_md: The fourth commandment continues into adult life: grown children should show their parents respect, gratitude and help, especially in old age, sickness, loneliness or need.

question: Who is responsible for a child’s religious education?
answer_md: Parents are the first educators of their children in the faith. They teach above all by example, prayer at home and taking their children to Mass. Parishes and schools help, but they do not replace the parents.

question: Is Halloween a Catholic celebration?
answer_md: The word Halloween comes from “All Hallows’ Eve”, the eve of All Saints’ Day (1 November), followed by All Souls’ Day (2 November). Catholics can keep its Christian meaning by remembering the saints, praying for the dead, and avoiding anything that glorifies evil or the occult.

question: Why is the Rosary so repetitive?
answer_md: The repeated Hail Marys are like a gentle background, freeing the heart to meditate on the mysteries of Jesus’ life with Mary. Saint John Paul II called the Rosary a contemplation of Christ’s face with Mary. Repetition is natural to love, as in the Psalms.

question: What is the Miraculous Medal?
answer_md: The Miraculous Medal was designed according to a vision of Mary given to Saint Catherine Labouré in Paris in 1830. It bears the prayer “O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.” It is a sacramental: its power comes from faith and prayer, not from the medal itself.

question: What is the Saint Benedict medal?
answer_md: The Saint Benedict medal carries an image of Saint Benedict and Latin initials of prayers asking God’s protection against evil, such as “Begone, Satan!” Worn with faith, it is a sacramental reminding us to reject sin and trust in Christ.

question: What is a chaplet?
answer_md: A chaplet is a set of prayers prayed on beads, often shorter than the Rosary, such as the Chaplet of Divine Mercy or the Chaplet of Saint Michael. Chaplets help us pray with focus and perseverance.

question: What are the Stations of the Cross?
answer_md: The Stations (or Way) of the Cross are fourteen moments of Jesus’ Passion, from his condemnation to his burial. Catholics pray them by meditating at each station, especially on Fridays of Lent, walking with Jesus in love and gratitude.

question: What is a holy hour?
answer_md: A holy hour is an hour of prayer, often before the Blessed Sacrament, recalling Jesus’ words in Gethsemane: “Could you not watch one hour with me?” It can include silent prayer, Scripture, the Rosary or simply resting in the Lord’s presence.

question: What are the First Fridays and First Saturdays?
answer_md: The First Fridays devotion honours the Sacred Heart by receiving Communion on the first Friday of nine consecutive months, as Jesus asked Saint Margaret Mary. The First Saturdays devotion, asked for at Fatima, offers Confession, Communion, the Rosary and meditation on five first Saturdays in reparation to Mary’s Immaculate Heart.

question: What is spiritual direction?
answer_md: Spiritual direction is regular conversation with a wise priest, religious or trained lay person who helps you grow in prayer, discern God’s will and live your faith more deeply. It is not counselling or Confession, though it may encourage both.

question: What is a retreat?
answer_md: A retreat is time set apart, from a few hours to several days, to step away from daily busyness and spend time with God in silence, prayer, Scripture and often the sacraments. Many parishes, monasteries and retreat houses offer them.

question: Who was Saint Nicholas, and is he Santa Claus?
answer_md: Saint Nicholas was a 4th-century bishop of Myra, in present-day Turkey, famous for his generosity, especially secret gifts to the poor. The figure of Santa Claus grew out of his memory. His feast is 6 December.
